title: Metrics with Meter: counters, histograms, gauges
summary: Pick the right instrument, keep attributes bounded, measure durations in seconds, and shape histograms with views.

steps.title: Five instruments, one question each
body: `System.Diagnostics.Metrics.Meter` is .NET's metrics API (the SDK listens with `.WithMetrics(m => m.AddMeter("Orders.Api"))`).
Pick the instrument by the question you will ask of it:
| Instrument | Records | Example | Prometheus shows it as |
| `Counter<long>` | increments that only go up | orders placed | `app_orders_total`, use `rate()` |
| `Histogram<double>` | a distribution of values | checkout duration in **seconds** | `_bucket`, `_sum`, `_count`, use `histogram_quantile()` |
| `UpDownCounter<long>` | increments up and down | carts open right now | a gauge |
| `ObservableGauge<T>` | a value read when exported | queue depth, cache size | a gauge |
| `ObservableCounter<T>` | a total you already keep | bytes sent by a library | a counter |
```csharp
static readonly Meter Meter = new("Orders.Api", "2.1.0");
static readonly Counter<long> Orders = Meter.CreateCounter<long>("app.orders", unit: "{order}");
static readonly Histogram<double> Duration = Meter.CreateHistogram<double>("app.checkout.duration", unit: "s");
Orders.Add(1, new("app.payment.method", "card"), new("app.order.status", "placed"));
Duration.Record(elapsed.TotalSeconds, new KeyValuePair<string, object?>("app.payment.method", "card"));
Every distinct combination of attribute values is its own **time series**. `app.payment.method` (3 values) × `app.order.status`
(2 values) is 6 series. Add `app.customer.id` and it is millions: that is the lab's task 9. Attributes on metrics must be
**bounded**; per-request detail goes on spans. In DI-heavy code, create meters through `IMeterFactory` so tests can isolate them.

pairs: how long each payment call took

steps.prompt: A `MeterListener` (what the SDK uses underneath) sums what a counter records. What does this print?
code: using var listener = new MeterListener { InstrumentPublished = (i, l) => { if (i.Meter.Name == "Demo") l.EnableMeasurementEvents(i); } };
steps.explain: The listener enabled every instrument of the `Demo` meter, including `app.refunds`, created after it started (`InstrumentPublished` fires for it too): 1 + 2 + 5. Without any listener, `Add` is a cheap no-op, like `StartActivity` returning null.

steps.title: Views: shape what is exported
body: A **view** changes how the SDK aggregates an instrument, without touching the code that records it: rename it, drop attributes,
or pick histogram buckets.
```csharp
.WithMetrics(m => m
.AddMeter("Orders.Api")
.AddView("app.checkout.duration", new ExplicitBucketHistogramConfiguration
Boundaries = [0.005, 0.01, 0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5],   // seconds: where your SLO threshold must be a boundary
TagKeys = ["app.payment.method"],                                // keep only these attributes
.AddView("legacy.*", MetricStreamConfiguration.Drop))
- **Buckets decide precision.** `histogram_quantile` interpolates inside a bucket, so an SLO of "95% under 300 ms" needs a boundary at
0.3. The default boundaries are in milliseconds-like steps up to 10 000, wrong for seconds (the HTTP instrumentation sets its own).
- In .NET 9+ the instrument itself can advise buckets: `CreateHistogram<double>(..., advice: new InstrumentAdvice<double> {
HistogramBucketBoundaries = [...] })`; a view still wins.
- **Exponential (base-2) histograms** (`Base2ExponentialBucketHistogramConfiguration`) pick buckets automatically with bounded relative
error; Prometheus 3 stores them as **native histograms**. Worth it once your backend supports them end to end.
- `TagKeys` is the emergency brake for cardinality: deploy it when a label explodes, then fix the code.

steps.prompt: Your SLO is "99% of checkouts complete within 400 ms". The histogram's boundaries are `0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1`. What is the problem?
options: There is no boundary at 0.4, so the share of requests under 400 ms can only be estimated by interpolating inside the 0.25-0.5 bucket
The SLO needs a counter, not a histogram
steps.explain: Count-based SLIs read `_bucket{le="0.4"}` directly: that series only exists if 0.4 is a boundary. Put SLO thresholds on bucket boundaries, with a view or instrument advice.

steps.title: Fix the buckets and the cardinality with a view
prompt: Another team's library records `lib.request.duration` (seconds) with the attributes `lib.tenant` and `lib.request.id`. You cannot
change it (it is in the starter, pretend it is a NuGet package). Register its meter **`Vendor.Lib`** and add **one view** on
- the histogram's boundaries are exactly **`0.05, 0.1, 0.4, 1`** (your SLO is 400 ms);
- only **`lib.tenant`** is kept as an attribute (`lib.request.id` makes one series per request).
**Run checks** calls `GET /lib` a few times and reads the exported histogram.
starter: public static readonly Histogram<double> Duration = Meter.CreateHistogram<double>("lib.request.duration", unit: "s");
solution: public static readonly Histogram<double> Duration = Meter.CreateHistogram<double>("lib.request.duration", unit: "s");
template: public static async Task Run(HttpClient http)
for (var i = 0; i < 6; i++) await http.GetAsync("/lib");
Dojo.Eq("one series per tenant, none per request", 2, pts.Count);
Dojo.Check("only lib.tenant is kept", pts.All(p => p.Tags.Keys.SequenceEqual(new[] { "lib.tenant" })), string.Join(", ", pts.SelectMany(p => p.Tags.Keys).Distinct()));
Dojo.Eq("all six requests are under 0.4 s", 6L, pts.Sum(p => p.Buckets.Take(3).Sum()));
Dojo.Eq("three were under 0.1 s", 3L, pts.Sum(p => p.Buckets.Take(2).Sum()));
